audio_caption: The clip begins with upbeat music, setting an energetic tone. A male voice introduces the segment as "Triple Trouble" and states his name is Chef. Another male voice identifies himself as Steve, and Chef explains that Steve will demonstrate how to make a knocking point and its placement. The energetic music stops. Steve begins a tutorial on positioning a knocking point, discussing necessary materials like arrows, bare shafts, thread, a bow square, a lighter, a knife, and super glue. He explains how to position the bow square to determine the arrow rest point, noting lines on the tool representing millimeters. Steve describes his starting point for the knocking point as eight, and explains how this will be the starting point to test what works best.

The clip begins with a male speaker stating, "you're gonna need" and describes using small pieces of thread, beginning with the bottom knocking point. He mentions placing it at eight, takes the bow square off, and creates a few small knots, commenting, "because this is not my... perfect knocking point yet." He indicates making three or four small knots for now. Then, he says an arrow is needed for the knock and demonstrates how to use it, pressing against the knock until it's all the way down, adjusting the knocking point.

The audio clip begins with speech, where a male speaker describes a process involving thread, mentioning "the other piece of thread" and the importance of keeping it "nice and tight." He then states he will take "the knock off" and continue putting in "the knots," explaining they should be placed in the same way as the lower knocking point, stating, "three or four that's enough for testing." Following this, the speaker says, "that's it" and indicates the need for a knife, which introduces the sound of cutting as he states he is going "to cut all the pieces off."

The audio begins with a male speaker stating, "Now we're going to turn around the bow." The speaker then explains that small pieces are being burned off and that it is important to turn the bow, otherwise the flame could damage the serving. Next, he sets up the bow and says he's going to shoot at 30m to see where they are. Finally, the distinct sound of an arrow being shot from a bow can be heard.

The clip starts with a male speaker describing his archery group. He then states that his arrows were not in the group and he is going to redo his nocking point. Before doing so, he makes sure to put the flat side of his knife against the serving to get straight cuttings into the nocking point. The sound of cutting is then heard, followed by what sounds like someone hitting something with a hammer, multiple times.

The audio clip starts with one male speaker, presenting information about a group, perhaps related to an activity, mentioning "we have a good group" and then distinguishing between a "red nocks" group and a "green nocks" group. He explains that this is how he wants his "knocking point." He states that "everything is set."

The clip starts with a male speaker introducing the topic of putting a nocking point on a bow. The speaker adopts a friendly, instructional tone, announcing that the bow will soon be ready to shoot. He then explains the procedure, detailing how he intends to do the same thing as before, involving putting the bow square on. The speaker highlights that the difference this time is that he will be making a nocking point with 15 knots instead of four. The speech is interrupted with sound of a snipping or cutting action.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker saying, "To make sure, I have a perfect knocking point", before describing his intention to create one with "15 knots". He mentions each knot will be on a different side of the string. The speaker continues with this description while there's an ambient sound, potentially background music, alongside the sounds associated with the crafting of the knots.

The clip starts with a male speaker providing instruction, "I'm gonna put on the super glue." He advises letting it dry for 15 minutes to avoid a fire hazard when burning it off later. He then states that any store-bought superglue is fine, not needing to be archery specific. This is followed by the sound of multiple clanking objects, presumably metallic. Background music, in a reggae style with a relaxed tone, also starts.

The audio clip begins with two male speakers discussing Steve's "knocking point" and the tuning process. One speaker suggests viewers "stay tuned" and subscribe for future tuning videos, concluding with "see you next time" and "see you." This is followed by an instrumental song with an upbeat and positive mood, and a driving rhythm, featuring a prominent electric bass. Shortly after, a sound suggesting a bow being drawn and released on a string or bow is heard.
